subject.title: [Bug]: TLS certificate pin mismatch loop when connecting through Cloudflare Tunnel/Access (anycast edge certs)

question: Should iOS Remote Domain connections to system-trusted public hostnames use standard PKI and hostname verification instead of mandatory leaf-certificate pinning?
rationale: The present pin protects against endpoint substitution but is incompatible with legitimate anycast and reverse-proxy certificate rotation; choosing which endpoint classes retain pinning changes the documented security boundary.

options.title: Use PKI for Remote Domain
options.body: For manual public domains, trust the system-validated chain and hostname while retaining explicit pinning for discovered, self-signed, or explicitly pinned endpoints.

options.title: Keep pinning with a pin set
options.body: Preserve mandatory pinning but support multiple bounded fingerprints or another operator-controlled identity set, which is more complex and may still be fragile with CDN-managed keys.

options.title: Keep current leaf pinning
options.body: Retain the strongest existing endpoint pin but document Cloudflare anycast and rotating reverse proxies as unsupported for the native app.

recommendation.title: Use PKI for Remote Domain
recommendation.body: For manual public domains, trust the system-validated chain and hostname while retaining explicit pinning for discovered, self-signed, or explicitly pinned endpoints.

likelyOwner.reason: The choice changes the security model established by the explicit-trust and TLS-pin hardening commits.
